description: F# library for Azure Quantum with quantum-first optimization (Graph Coloring, TSP, MaxCut, Knapsack, Network Flow, Portfolio), Azure Quantum backend integration (IonQ, Rigetti, Quantinuum, Atom Computing), extensible circuit validation, local quantum simulation, QAOA with automatic parameter optimization (Nelder-Mead), OpenQASM 2.0 support, error mitigation techniques (ZNE, PEC, REM), Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG), and educational quantum algorithms (Grover, QFT, Amplitude Amplification, QPE, Shor, HHL) and quantum chemistry (VQE, QPE) with cloud backend execution as whole-circuit jobs. Native IQuantumBackend integration for IonQ, Rigetti, Quantinuum, Atom Computing, IQM and D-Wave, plus Pasqal neutral-atom analog hardware (via Pulser) and a neutral-atom analog programming model; additional platforms (IBM, Amazon Braket, Google Cirq) are targetable via OpenQASM 2.0 export/import.
releaseNotes:
v1.4.15: cloud results keep their recorded shots; a local Azure Quantum service; honest error bars

- FIXED (cloud results; the 1.4.14 known limitation): a cloud backend's returned state carries the job's recorded counts (QuantumState.withRecordedCounts, tryRecordedCounts, recordedShotCount, recordedShots; UnifiedBackend.recordedShots, recordedShotCount). QuantumState.measure and UnifiedBackend.measureState on such a state return the job's own shots, drawn without replacement and never more than it measured, instead of drawing new outcomes from its histogram with a pseudo-random generator. The array can be shorter than requested: Grover, Bernstein–Vazirani, Deutsch–Jozsa and VQC take frequencies over the shots measured (Grover reported 1,000 measurements from a 500-shot job). MeasurementHistogram states behave the same way, and Braket results carry their counts too
- CHANGED (cloud results): a job's recorded shots come in an order seeded from the counts themselves, so a run against a seeded simulator (LocalQuantumService Seed) repeats exactly; the order was taken from process-wide randomness
- FIXED (error mitigation): the strategy selected for a high accuracy requirement had a fallback with a ZNE component, which applyStrategy refuses on a finished histogram like the primary, so applying the recommended strategy was always an Error; the fallback is readout correction alone
- FIXED (whole-circuit trials): a job whose histogram keys are narrower than the packed circuit (unpadded legacy result payloads) is widened with zeros instead of throwing from WholeCircuit.runTrials
- FIXED (Shor): each period-finding attempt reads a distinct measured shot. On a cloud backend the attempts walk the job's recorded shots one by one and a further job is submitted only when all of them have been tried; they used to re-read the one finished job, so a one-shot backend spent all 16 attempts on a single outcome. A 100-shot backend covers 16 attempts with one job
- FIXED (Shor): periods come from the continued-fraction convergents of the measured outcome (and their multiples below N), the smallest r with a^r ≡ 1 (mod N). The old post-processing picked the fraction with denominator up to N closest to the phase, which is not a convergent: with the 6 counting qubits that fit N = 21 the outcome 11/64 matched 3/17 instead of 1/6, so the period of 2 mod 21 was almost never found and Shor.factor21 failed
- CHANGED (BB84, E91): the whole-circuit route groups trials by kind (BB84: Alice's bit and basis, Eve's basis, Bob's basis; E91: the three bases) and runs each kind in slots side by side on disjoint qubits, so every shot of every job is used (new WholeCircuit.runTrials, TrialKind, trialWidth, MaxTrialWidth = 16). A 200-bit BB84 key on a 100-shot backend takes 1 job (was 68) and at most 2 with Eve (was 135); E91 over 600 pairs takes 2 jobs (was 100) and at most 9 with Eve. With one shot per job the job count is as before
- FIXED (BB84, E91): circuits are packed to the backend's runnable width instead of a fixed 12 qubits, so both run on the 8-qubit density-matrix simulator. NoisyLocalBackend now declares its 8-qubit limit (IQubitLimitedBackend)
- FIXED (E91): on the gate-by-gate route Eve measured Alice's and Bob's qubits as two independent samples of the Bell state; it is now one joint measurement, so her two outcomes agree as they must
- CHANGED (teleportation): the whole-circuit route runs the Z, X and Y tomography settings as three copies of the protocol side by side in one 9-qubit circuit: one job per call instead of three. BobState is the Z copy's 3-qubit state
- FIXED (whole-circuit oracles): an oracle the whole-circuit route cannot read is always an Error. An unknown closure used to be probed with an empty state and treated as the identity when it returned that state unchanged, so a closure that branches on its input could be submitted as no gates and a balanced oracle reported constant. Oracles that carry their gates are the new WholeCircuit.GateOracle (built by gateOracle, and the new identityOracle), recognised by type; DeutschJozsa.constantZeroOracle and constantOneOracle are identityOracle
- ADDED: CircuitBuilder.mapQubits and WholeCircuit.shiftOps place a gate list on other qubits
- ADDED (LocalQuantumService): an optional local HTTP service that emulates the Azure Quantum workspace REST API (job submit, status, cancel, list, SAS blob storage, bearer-token checks) and runs each job on the local simulator, so the cloud backends' full Azure path — transpilation, IonQ JSON, Quil and OpenQASM serialisation, job lifecycle, result download and parsing — can be tested without sending data to Azure. IonQ, Rigetti, Quantinuum, IQM and Atom Computing targets are supported; programs it cannot decode fail as the provider would; failures and rejected submissions can be injected. LocalQuantumService.start, CreateHttpClient, WorkspaceUrl, Jobs, Requests (docs/local-quantum-service.md)
- FIXED (Rigetti, Quantinuum, IQM, Atom Computing): circuits were submitted without measurements — Quil declared ro but never MEASUREd into it, and OpenQASM for a unitary circuit had no measure — so a real provider would have read out nothing. A circuit that measures no qubit is now measured in full at the end (CloudBackendHelpers.withTerminalMeasurements); CircuitBuilder.Measure converts to MEASURE q ro[q]
- FIXED (Rigetti, Quantinuum results): RigettiBackend.parseRigettiResults reads Azure's per-shot ro register (rigetti.quil-results.v1) and QuantinuumBackend.parseQuantinuumResult the per-shot c register (honeywell.quantum-results.v1); both read only an aggregated histogram before. The aggregated shapes are still accepted
- ADDED (tests): end-to-end tests run Grover, Shor, BB84, E91, teleportation, the oracle protocols, QRNG, Primitives and job budgets through the real cloud backend classes against LocalQuantumService, pinning each answer and the number of jobs submitted
- FIXED (quantum Monte Carlo): QuantumMonteCarlo.estimateExpectation reports the Cramér–Rao standard error of the maximum-likelihood amplitude-estimation fit (≈0.0013 for a = 0.25 at 1,000 shots) instead of 1/GroverIterations (0.25). The fit is solved to the exact maximum instead of stopping at its 1.6e-5 rad grid, so exact-simulator estimates are exact to about 1e-8
- ADDED (quantum Monte Carlo, option pricing): amplitude estimation reads a topological backend's logical-qubit probabilities, so QMC, option pricing and the risk engine run on topological backends (a European call prices at the simulator's value on the Ising backend)
- CHANGED (option pricing, different results): the price grid uses the conditional mean of each equal-probability bin (new StatisticalDistributions.discretizeLogNormalBinMeans) instead of the mid-bin quantile, which keeps E[S] exact. With the fit fix, 6-qubit prices on the exact simulator match Black–Scholes to about 0.04% (were 0.4–1.7% low), Vega to 0.1% (was −1.3%) and Rho to 2.5% or better (was up to 5.6%); Gamma is limited by the price grid (8 qubits: 0.06%, was −4.6%)
- CHANGED (ADAPT-VQE, ADAPT-QAOA): on shot-sampling (cloud) backends a run is capped by the new MaxCloudJobs config field (default Some 2000; None = no cap). A run whose first operator or layer cannot fit is refused with a MaxCloudJobs ValidationError before any job; otherwise it stops before an iteration that could cross the cap and returns the best ansatz so far with JobCapReached = true. estimateCloudJobs gives the plan (a 3-qubit toy submitted 9,730 jobs uncapped). Results add EnergyStandardError (None on exact backends) and CloudJobs. solveQubo keeps one job of the cap for its final sample
- CHANGED (quantum kernels): on a shot-sampling backend, a shots argument different from the backend's Shots is an Error naming both (as Primitives.sample), returned before any job; it was silently ignored. This also applies to SimilaritySearch, AnomalyDetection and QuantumKernelSVM on cloud backends. Exact simulators still sample shots
- ADDED (HHL): HHL.executeWithRelativePhases recovers the signs and relative phases of the solution on whole-circuit (cloud) backends with interference circuits: one Hadamard circuit per solution qubit (plus one RX(π/2) circuit per qubit for complex systems), 1 + log₂N jobs for a real system. New readout HhlReadout.MeasuredRelativePhases (a new union case). On backends with state access it equals HHL.execute
- CHANGED (HHL regression): QuantumRegressionHHL.train works on cloud backends: it measures the weights' signs with executeWithRelativePhases (1 + log₂ of the padded dimension jobs per fit, e.g. 3 for 4 weights) and recovers the scale by the same least-squares fit as on the simulator; it returned an Error there before. The simulator path is unchanged. New field RegressionResult.Circuits
